items.text: Once you move your mover to a new location, your turn has officially begun. To keep tournament play running smoothly, you can take back your move (and go to a different location) only if you have NOT yet taken any action at the new location. If you have taken even one action there, you must stay and carry on with your remaining actions.
You can't play a Condition unless you can do exactly what its text says.
A Hero with 0 Strength can be defeated with a Vanquish action without using Allies. You can still use Allies if you want; in that case they are not discarded after the Vanquish.
Items, Allies and Heroes can't be played or moved to locked locations. Items can't be attached to Heroes or Allies at locked locations, and Items at locked locations can't be activated.
No value in the game can go below zero.
When a card tells you to FIND another card, look first in the Realm, then in the matching discard pile, then in the matching deck.

To be fair to your opponents, when you retrieve a card of a specific category (Effect, Ally, etc.) from a discard pile or a deck, show it to them to prove it's the right kind. If you can retrieve any card, you don't need to show it.

Cards that reveal from a deck until a card of a specific type is found can loop forever if no copies of that card are left in the deck or discard pile. In that case the card can still be played, but its only effect is to reshuffle that whole deck, discard pile included.

Conditions that trigger when an opponent discards cards can be used only when the opponent discards cards from their hand, either with the Discard Cards action or through other cards' effects (such as the Evil Queen's Magic Tomes). Discarding cards in any other way doesn't trigger them.

general.title: Cards that make you lose tokens
general.intro: Prospero Hall era cards are read as below, as clarified by designer Stephanie Straw. Ravensburger era cards are read as below because designer Mike Mulvihill hasn't clarified them.

items.text: Lose up to 2 Power.
Evil Queen loses up to 1 Poison.
Yzma loses up to 2 Power.
Mother Gothel loses up to 2 Trust.
Lose 2 Power, and exactly 2.
items.source: No clarification from designer Mike Mulvihill

items.text: Tamatoa loses 3 Power, and exactly 3.
items.source: No clarification from designer Mike Mulvihill

general.title: Cards worded with “any”
general.intro: These cards say “any” in the original English text. Read them as follows.

items.text: “any Allies to any other location”: move any number of Allies to one single location.
“all Heroes”: move all Heroes.
“any location”: discard a Cauldron Born from one single location.
“each Hero to any other location”: move each Hero to one single location.
“any Hero”: move exactly one Hero.
“any Hero”: move exactly one Hero (or Buzz Lightyear, whether Guardian or Ally).
“any Ally”: discard exactly one Ally.
“all Heroes to any other locations”: move all Heroes, possibly each to a different location.
“any Transformation”: defeat exactly one Transformation.
“any Transformation”: move exactly one Transformation.
“any Hero”: move exactly one Hero.
“any action”: take exactly one action.
“any number of Allies”: move any number of Allies.
“any other Hero”: must be defeated before defeating any single other Hero.
“any of your three available actions”: you can take all, none or only some of them.
“any number”: move any number of Allies.
“all… to any other locations”: move all Heroes and Allies, possibly each to a different location.
“any Hero”: move exactly one Hero.
“any card”: move exactly one card.

general.title: Cards that give access to unavailable actions
general.intro: Some cards let you take actions that are normally unavailable: covered by Heroes or tokens, locked, already taken, or at another location. Some give access to the action, ignoring what blocks it; others let you take the action directly, through the card itself.

items.text: Lets you take an action at another location. Maleficent can take it again if she then moves to that location.
Lets you take an action at an adjacent location. The same action can be taken again with a second copy of Grow Giant.
Lets you take an action at Evil Queen's location, even if it has already been taken.
Lets you take a covered action. The same action can be taken again with another copy of Bravo! Bravo!.

items.term: Sir Hiss, Whatever It Takes, I'll Fix Ya!, Trapped
items.villain: Prince John, Cruella de Vil, Evil Queen, Tamatoa
items.text: These give access to an action covered by a Hero, as if that Hero weren't there. So the action counts as taken, and you can't take it again if the Hero covering it is moved or defeated.

Captain Hook.text: If Peter Pan is the first card revealed during a Fate action, the other card must be revealed too, because both are revealed at the same time.

Maleficent.text: If Fauna is played to a location with two Dreamless Sleep, only one copy is discarded.

If Forest of Thorns and Dreamless Sleep are at the same location and a Hero with 4 or more Strength is played there, Forest of Thorns is discarded. Then the Hero gets -2 Strength from Dreamless Sleep.

Jafar.text: Its trigger (an opponent has two or more Items in their Realm) also counts Fate Items. It doesn't start a Fate action, so it doesn't trigger Conditions that react to a Fate action.
Each hypnotized Hero counts as an Ally for other players' Conditions. For consistency with similar mechanics, hypnotized Heroes move to the bottom of the board, at the same location.
Both actions are optional: you can play the card without taking either of them.
If Abu is played to Aladdin's location (or vice versa), Abu can NOT take an Item already attached to Aladdin (and vice versa).

Prince John.text: Moving an Ally is optional, but the Vanquish action is mandatory. The Ally you moved doesn't have to take part in the Vanquish (the Italian edition is worded inaccurately).
Sir Hiss lets you take a covered action only once. You can't take that action again even if the Hero covering it is defeated.
When the targeted Hero is defeated, the Power “returns” to Prince John rather than being “gained”, so it doesn't count for cards triggered by gaining Power.

If Robin Hood is already in the Realm when Maid Marian is defeated and he holds Power stolen with Steal from the Rich, that Power goes back to the Cauldron, not to Prince John. If Maid Marian is defeated by an Ally with the Golden Arrow, Robin Hood is found before the Golden Arrow's Power is gained, so you gain only 1 Power.
If the Golden Arrow is attached to an Ally used to defeat Robin Hood, you gain 2 Power, because Robin Hood leaves the Realm before the Golden Arrow's effect triggers.
Power that “returns” to Prince John from a Hero targeted by Steal from the Rich is NOT affected by Robin Hood, so you don't get 1 Power less. The same goes for Power stolen by Little John.

Queen of Hearts.text: If a Shrunk Hero shares a location with other Heroes, it is the only Hero there that covers an action. The others cover nothing until the Shrunk Hero is defeated or moved.
Size effects take priority in this order: Enlarged, then Shrunk, then Normal.

When a Hero is Shrunk or Enlarged, the player doing it (Queen of Hearts, or an opponent through a Fate action) chooses which action it covers. The covered actions can't change until the Hero returns to normal and is Shrunk or Enlarged again.

Shrunk and Enlarged Heroes ALWAYS have effect and can involve the same location AT THE SAME TIME, even several at once. An “altered” Hero always covers the actions it has to cover: 1 for Shrunk Heroes, 3 for Enlarged Heroes.

Enlarged and Normal Heroes CAN involve the same location and both cover actions there. For example, with one Hero at the Courtyard and one at the Hedge Maze, if the Courtyard Hero is Enlarged, both Hedge Maze actions are covered (one by the Enlarged Hero, both by the Normal Hero).

Shrunk and Normal Heroes CAN'T involve the same location. If one or more Shrunk Heroes are at a location, any Normal Hero there covers no actions until the Shrunk Heroes are moved or defeated. If two Heroes are already at a location and one of them is Shrunk, slide the Normal Hero up so it does NOT cover both actions, leaving uncovered the one the Shrunk Hero freed.
Can only Shrink normal-sized Heroes; it can't return Enlarged Heroes to normal.

Dr. Facilier.text: Triggers when an opponent discards two or more cards from their hand, through the Discard Cards action or other cards' effects. They don't have to be discarded all at once. Playing an Effect doesn't count as discarding a card, and neither does discarding Allies used in a Vanquish.
The Power needed to trigger this Condition doesn't have to be gained all at once.

Evil Queen.text: Can be used even if there is more than one Hero at that location.

The Fate card and the Poison token are drawn and gained only once the Fate action is over, not before. Drawing a card with Magic Mirror stays optional despite the card text, as stated in the Villain Guide.
Can be played if Evil Queen has no Poison, but not if there are no Heroes in the discard pile.

Hades.text: When moved two locations, Titans skip any location in between (so they avoid the abilities of Heroes placed there) and can use their ability only once, because it is a single move.
Moving a Titan with Pegasus triggers its ability.
Titans are not Allies, so they don't trigger other players' Conditions that refer to Allies.

Scar.text: It can't be put into your own hand, because it goes to the discard pile only after its Effect is over.

The Fate cards looked at can both be discarded, both kept, or one discarded and one kept. If you have two copies of Injustice in hand and want to play them, you must play both at the same time and resolve them one at a time.
His ability works only when other Hyenas are discarded from his location. If Banzai himself is discarded, you gain no Power.

If a Hero with Rafiki's Stick attached is defeated, it does NOT trigger other players' Conditions based on defeating Heroes (such as Ursula's Arrogance) because, per the rulebook, a Hero is defeated when it is discarded from the Realm after a Vanquish action or a card's effect.

Ratigan.text: The Item or Ally to move must be at the Airship's location.
Ratigan.source: Card text (the Italian edition omits “at its location”)

Yzma.text: Yzma can choose to take one, all or none of Beauty Sleep's actions at the start of her next turn. A Cruel Irony can play this card only if it is the first and only action of the turn.
Watch out for the misprint in some editions: it's 3 or more to defeat a Hero with 3 or less.
If Kronk becomes a Hero with the Dagger already attached, the Dagger stays attached to him at the top of the Realm. When Kronk is discarded from the Realm, the Dagger returns to the player's hand.
Read Chicha as “loses UP TO 2 Power”: if Yzma has fewer than 2 Power when she moves to Chicha's location, she loses them all.
When Kronk reaches 3 Power and moves to the top of the Realm, the Power stays on him, because The Path That Rocks can collect it at any time.

If it is the only card left in the Fate decks: choose a Hero from the discard pile; shuffle the discard pile, without the chosen Hero and Beware the Groove, to form four new decks; shuffle the chosen Hero into up to two decks; discard Beware the Groove (its effect is resolved).
Fate cards that shuffle one or more decks can also target the deck they were drawn from. If no card in a Fate deck can be played, the deck is reshuffled and put back. No card is discarded.

Pete.text: If you play more than one Bandit through its ability, you still pay the cost of each Bandit.
Taking a card from the discard pile is optional.
His ability swaps two Goal tokens that are next to each other.

If Pete spends 6 Power with Mickey Mouse in the Realm, Power Play can't be completed. But if Pete spends part of the 6 Power, defeats Mickey Mouse and then spends the rest, Power Play can be completed.

Mother Gothel.text: Can also be triggered when an Item or Ally is moved during a Fate action, and when a Hero with an Item attached is moved.

Mother Gothel.term: Everyone Has a Dream & Now I'm the Bad Guy
Mother Gothel.text: The usual rule applies: you must be able to do what the card says to play it. If Mother Gothel has no Trust to lose, they can't be played.
Can be played even if Mother Gothel has fewer than two Trust. If he is defeated, Mother Gothel still gains 2 Trust.

Gaston.text: Every extra action granted by other opponents' cards counts toward the minimum of four needed to trigger Beautiful as Me. If the last of the four opponent actions is a Fate action (against Gaston or another player), wait for it to finish before playing Beautiful as Me.
Revealed Fate cards that aren't Heroes are not discarded: shuffle them back into the Fate deck. If the Hero played by Take Me Instead is Belle, you can't remove an Obstacle.
Unlike Come Into the Light, it doesn't say “up to”. So Get Out! removes exactly 3 Obstacles.
Lefou's ability is mandatory, so the Allies used in the Vanquish return to the player's hand, Lefou included if he took part.
If Maurice's Invention is attached to a Hero, when Mrs. Potts and Chip are played it can be attached to any other Hero.

If the other revealed Fate card can't be played, or The Rose was revealed through Jafar's Deception or Ursula's Trickery, you can still resolve The Rose's full text. The Rose is discarded after the other revealed Fate card is played. So if the discard pile must be reshuffled to draw two more Fate cards, The Rose is shuffled in with it and can be drawn again.
His ability is mandatory, even if Gaston played him through Take Me Instead. So any number of Allies at the location where Beast is played must be moved to one single location.
Can be played ONLY if at least one Obstacle is missing from every location. If even one location still has both Obstacles, It Is You can't be played.
When Maurice is played and Maurice's Invention is found, the Invention can be attached to him or to any other Hero at his location.
It's an Item to attach to a Hero: if there are no Heroes in the Realm, it can't be played. Ignore the Strength value in the bottom-left corner, it's a misprint.

The exact purpose of this card is still unclear. Suggested use: remove an Obstacle if Beast is in play, or replace one if Belle is in play, to set up cards that remove a given number of Obstacles at once. Played while both Beast and Belle are in play, it only gives back the Power spent to play it.
Can be used to replace even a single Obstacle at a single location, because the original text says “all”.

Lady Tremaine.text: It isn't shuffled into the reshuffled deck.

You can choose a card that can't be played, cancelling the Fate. If you choose an Effect, the Fating player decides how to apply it. If you choose a Hero, Lady Tremaine chooses where to play it, but the Fating player resolves its effects. This card can't override the restrictions of The Prince, the Glass Slipper and Ball Gown Cinderella.

Every Hero that shares Lucifer's location at any moment, whether the Hero or Lucifer is moved or played there, is Trapped. The Trapped token stays on the Hero even when Lucifer is moved or discarded from the Trapped Hero's location.
Can be played even if Cinderella isn't in play. Ball Gown Cinderella can be moved but not Trapped.
Lady Tremaine.source: Mike Mulvihill, designer; confirmed by Lord of the Board, playtester
Lord of the Board and other playtesters

Lady Tremaine.text: The only cards that can be moved or played to The Ballroom are The Prince, Ball Gown Cinderella, Ball Gown Anastasia and Ball Gown Drizella. Items can't be played there either, otherwise they would escape Lucifer's protection and Jaq's effects.
When The Prince is revealed during a Fate action, he must be played immediately and the other revealed Fate card is discarded.
If Ball Gown Cinderella replaces a Trapped Cinderella, the Trapped token is removed, since Ball Gown Cinderella can't be Trapped.

Horned King.text: They can only be played by replacing Ancient Soldiers before the start of the Horned King's turn, if The Power of the Black Cauldron is showing. Their 0 Cost (top left) does NOT mean they can be played for free with a Play a Card action.
It isn't shuffled back in with the Fate discard pile.
The Fating player decides what the Horned King must do. If they choose discarding cards, the Horned King picks which ones. The Horned King can't lose Power if he has fewer than 2.

Madam Mim.text: Can defeat ONE of Merlin's Transformations, not all of them.
It isn't shuffled back in with the other cards in the Villain discard pile.
Can't be played if Merlin's Transformation deck is empty.

Lotso.text: See Endless searches in the general rules.
Wait for the Fate action to end before using this Condition. It isn't shuffled back in with the rest of the discard pile.
The other revealed cards are shuffled back into the Fate deck.
Can be played even if Big Baby isn't in Lotso's Realm.
Heroes can be moved to different locations, outside the Caterpillar Room.

When you play the Hat, put a -1 Strength token on every Hero except Woody. Rex gets -1 from Woody's Hat when he is the only Hero at a location (and keeps it when other Heroes are later played there), when all the other Heroes move away from his location, and when he is played to a location that already has other Heroes. If Bonnie's Toys is played while Woody's Hat is in play, add a -1 Strength token after applying Bonnie's Toys, except on Rex if he shares a location with other Heroes. When Woody's Hat is discarded, remove a -1 Strength token from every Hero in the Realm.
Lotso.source: Shared ruling with the US community (presumably playtester-approved)

Syndrome.text: Can't move Omnidroid v.10 while it's at the top of the Realm.
Refers to the actual cost the opponent paid for a card, not the printed cost.

It's always played at Downtown Metroville: at the top of the Realm if Syndrome's Remote isn't in play or Syndrome controls it, at the bottom if the Remote is attached to a Hero. Each time a Hero is played and the Remote is attached to it, Omnidroid v.10 moves to that location, at the bottom. When the Hero with the Remote is defeated, Omnidroid v.10 moves up at the same location and the Remote drops to the bottom. Technically, activating the Remote and flipping Omnidroid v.10 to its Destroyed side should be your last action to win. You can do it FIRST and THEN defeat the remaining Heroes, but it's not recommended: the Destroyed Omnidroid would stay at the top of the Realm for good, blocking actions, and could no longer be moved (as the Villain Guide says) or used to defeat the remaining Heroes.

Discard it before looking at the top six cards of the deck. If the other revealed Fate card can't be played, Teamwork can still be played. If two copies of Teamwork are revealed, they cancel each other out and only one copy is played. If the discard pile must be reshuffled to reveal six cards, Teamwork is NOT shuffled in, because its effect hasn't finished resolving.

Oogie Boogie.text: If It's a Vacation discards Jack Skellington, he counts as a Hero, since he wasn't played from the Fate deck.
If you use What Have We Here? and roll 8 or more, the Bats are not discarded, because What Have We Here?'s Effect is in play and finishes resolving before the Bats' one.
You can choose not to discard any card and still draw two.
Apply the -2 to the dice roll only after any other modifiers from other cards' abilities, Loaded Dice included. In other words, Hello, Oogie!'s -2 is the very last step to get the final result.

Can be played at Oogie Boogie's current location, even though her ability makes his mover go to Sally's location. Heroes can always be played to an unlocked location, whether or not their abilities can be fully resolved.

When the Mayor is defeated, Oogie Boogie reveals cards from the Fate deck and decides where to play the Hero found. Unused Fate cards are shuffled back into the deck. If Jack Skellington comes up, he must be played because he says Hero, but as an Effect, because he is played from the Fate deck. If Sally comes up and Oogie Boogie plays her at a different location, his mover must still go to Sally's location, and the turn continues with the actions available there.
Once defeated, he is shuffled into the deck; he doesn't have to go on top.

Shere Khan.text: Two copies can be played to take the same action in the same turn, because it's the card's Effect that lets you take the action: you aren't taking it directly.
Shere Khan.source: Shared ruling with the US community (presumably playtester-approved)

Shere Khan.text: If you choose not to play the revealed Ally, it is discarded with the other cards.
You can shuffle any number of cards into the deck, from 0 to 3, so Trust in Me is playable even with no discard pile.
If you use Bagheera's ability, you must move all Heroes and all Allies at Bagheera's location to other locations, not just some.
This card can always be chosen for a Fate action: choose a location and every Hero there gets +1 Strength. If there are no Heroes, just play and discard the card.
You can always choose this card and apply neither of its two effects, or only one.
More than one Fire token can be stacked on the same action.

King Candy.text: If Candy Cy-Bugs are targeted by Can't Be Allowed to Race, they don't move to another location and don't get +1 Strength, because that only happens when they're actually used in a Vanquish action that would discard them.
Can be played even if you have no Allies in play or don't want to move them.
For Turbo-Tastic, actions under the Racer token also count as covered.
You can choose to move no Allies (“any number” includes 0), but you must still be able to perform a Vanquish action to play it.

The card text can be misleading but, as the Villain Guide says, Pay to Race is played BEFORE moving King Candy's mover, and only AFTER resolving the Racer token's movement. So, in order: move the Racer token, play Pay to Race, then declare King Candy's movement and move him.

If cards move King Candy's mover or the Racer token back before the race begins, both need a full lap of the track to win. The Racer token covers the actions it sits on and prevents taking them. The Racer token stays where it is if all Glitches are removed from Vanellope.

Whether or not Vanellope already has a Glitch attached, King Candy's turn always ends as soon as a Glitch is played. If a Glitch makes King Candy and the Racer token cross the finish line at the same time, King Candy wins, since his name comes before the Racer token on the card.
Vanellope von Schweetz can be played at Ralph's location only if you defeat Ralph with the Medal attached. Defeating Wreck-It Ralph without the Medal has no effect.
The text says “up to four action spaces”, so you can play this card and not move King Candy at all.

Can be played even with no Candy Cy-Bugs in play: it asks you to choose a location and move there any Cy-Bugs at adjacent locations. The second part of the card is optional, so it doesn't stop you from playing it.
Can be played even with no Heroes in the discard pile, since it says “may”. So you can choose it as one of the two Fate options and not use its ability.

Davy Jones.term: The Crew of the Flying Dutchman & The Crew of the Black Pearl
Davy Jones.text: Their Strength changes are dynamic: remember to add or remove Strength tokens as Allies or Heroes come and go.
Can be played even with no Heroes left in the Fate deck; the result is rebuilding the whole Fate deck by shuffling in the discard pile.
The Ally discarded instead of First Mate Maccus must not have been involved in the Vanquish action.
Can be used to take a covered action.
Both sentences say “may”, so you can play this card without resolving its effects.
Her Strength bonus adds up for each Hero played after her, so she doesn't lose Strength if other Heroes leave the Realm.
If he has The Heart token attached when he is defeated, resolve James Norrington's effects first, then The Heart's: gain 2 Power first, then lose all your Power.
A Hero can't have more than one Treasure token. When a Hero with an unrevealed Treasure token is defeated, the token goes back face down to the supply.

Tamatoa.term: Crustacean With the Power of Creation
Tamatoa.text: Although the Italian edition says “shuffle”, read it as “you may shuffle”: the Italian edition missed the final revision of the text.
Can be played only at the end of an opponent's turn, if they took two or fewer actions.
Can be played only if you have at least three cards in your Villain discard pile.

To trigger this Condition, count opposing Allies' Strength as already modified by passive effects as soon as they enter the Realm, such as Scar's Hungry Hyenas (they enter with modified Strength if played where other Hyenas are) or Davy Jones' Crew of the Flying Dutchman (it enters with 4 Strength if there's at least one Ally at the other locations).

If an action is covered by both a Hero and Something Shiny, Trapped still can't let Tamatoa take it: it must be covered by a Hero only. If the covered action is at Tamatoa's location and the Hero covering it is defeated in the same turn, Tamatoa can NOT take that action a second time (if he already took it with Trapped).

While Tamatoa controls it and is the target of a Fate action, wait for the Fate action to end before gaining 2 Power. If Maui Time is played and Tamatoa loses control of the Hook, the 2 Power can't be gained.
If Maui's Hook is in Tamatoa's hand, it must still be taken and attached to Maui. If Maui has Strength tokens when he is found, they are discarded.
Strength tokens on Allies are not discarded. If Allies with the same name have different Strength tokens, redistribute them randomly.
If revealed through Not Exactly Maui Time, it must be played.
